topic: Cottage cheese (קוטג') shortage, attributed to protein-trend demand

cluster.headline: הטרנד שגרם למחסור תמידי על המדפים: "חוסרים בכל הארץ" הביקוש קפץ במיליונים
cluster.body_note: Plain curl returned HTTP 403 (226 bytes, no JSON-LD). Body read via WebFetch rendering. Byline: Hili Keren (הילי קרן), published 25.11.26 09:05, 'המהדורה המרכזית'. Topic: cottage cheese. Key data sentences: 'אם מסתכלים על הנתונים היבשים, מתברר שהמכירות של הקוטג' על שלל מותגיו אכן זינקו' / 'באוקטובר 2025 נמכרו יותר מ-7.5 מיליון יחידות' vs 'מעל 10 מיליון יחידות' in the equivalent month this year. There is no 'לפי נתוני' attribution anywhere. Other content: Tnuva attributes the shortages to rising demand; an unnamed senior industry source says there are shortages nationwide; consultant Moti Elbaz (Success Code) ties the demand to the protein trend; Shufersal, Victory and Yohananof raised the price by 3%. The body itself says the shortage began about six months earlier with a production malfunction at Tnuva's plant.

scope_determination.reasoning: Borderline. The article states a specific empirical claim (cottage-cheese unit sales, Oct 2025 >7.5M vs Oct 2026 >10M) framed as 'the dry data', but it names no source (no chain data, StoreNext/Nielsen, CBS, Dairy Board or Tnuva filing). It is not a detect exclusion (not a registry, event measurement, market/rates data or poll), and its content is not purely logistics/framing, so the spec's 'claims: []' route (zero judgable claims) does not fit. An unattributed figure presented as data is what source_not_found exists for ('cited only by the outlet'), so the unit figures are verdicted rather than dropped. Anecdotal/quoted content (shortages nationwide, protein-trend explanation by a consultant) is excluded as framing.

claims.claim: הביקוש קפץ במיליונים (demand jumped by millions)
claims.source_figure: No primary source located. The only basis is the article's own unattributed unit-sales figures (about 7.5M to about 10M units/month, roughly +2.5M or +33% YoY for October).
claims.note: Internally consistent with the body's figures, but those figures are unsourced. The headline also relabels unit SALES as DEMAND. During a documented shortage, sales are capped by supply and are not a measure of demand, so the label is unverifiable either way.

claims.claim: באוקטובר 2025 נמכרו יותר מ-7.5 מיליון יחידות קוטג'
claims.source_figure: Not located in any public dataset (StoreNext/Nielsen/CBS/Dairy Board/Tnuva searched in Hebrew and English).
claims.note: Presented as 'הנתונים היבשים' with no attribution. Possibly retail-panel data, but the outlet does not say so.

claims.claim: בחודש המקביל השנה (אוקטובר 2026) נמכרו מעל 10 מיליון יחידות קוטג'
claims.note: Same unattributed data sentence as claim 2. It is also notable as context: October 2026 was itself reported as a shortage month (holiday production gap, Swiss imports), which makes a record sales month plausible only with imports or multi-brand counting ('על שלל מותגיו'). Unverifiable.

claims.claim: Causal conclusion: a demand trend ('הטרנד') is what caused the permanent shelf shortage
claims.source_figure: The article's own body says the shortage began with a production malfunction at Tnuva's plant. External coverage (JPost, Walla, ice) attributes the 2026 shortages primarily to supply-side failures: the Alon Tavor automated-warehouse glitch from July 2026, lost holiday working days, and dairy disruptions. The demand explanation rests on Tnuva's own statement and one consultant.
claims.note: Low-to-moderate confidence; flag for blind QA. Rising demand may be real, but the headline presents it as THE cause while the body and the wider record show a supply shock as the trigger. This is a causal inference, so it falls under scope (a conclusion inferred from data), not pure framing.

claims.claim: שופרסל, ויקטורי ויוחננוף העלו את מחיר הקוטג' ב-3 אחוזים
claims.source_figure: Not located. Search found earlier 2026 reports of chains raising cottage prices beyond dairy announcements (jdn.co.il), but no 3% figure for these three chains.
claims.note: Unattributed in the article. The figure could be checked against the chains' price-transparency feeds (Price Transparency Law), which this audit did not parse.
